criteria.name: artwork_craft
criteria.why: Frames 1 and 2 pass the place-at-an-hour test: storm deck, caprock in haze, cured grass with contact, the pole line on 2 now reading as a line converging to the horizon. The rest lean on primitives or dead zones. Frame 3's heads are plain boxes on U brackets, the caprock is a flat red slab with a hard base edge, and the ground is a flat brown plane with sparse sticks. Frame 6's 33 heads read at full size as small dark icons, not the planned white housings, so the focal is weak. Frame 7's tubes are flat beige cylinders with no galvanized sheen. Frame 9's figure is a low-poly kit person with a flat shirt. On 1, 2 and 7 the caprock face shows the same repeated vertical shadow striping. Frames 4 and 5 are finished: paper with a cast shadow on grained veneer, binders, window edge. Frame 8's chair field is convincing, but its top third is an unlit black wall standing in for a plate.

criteria.name: deck_coherence
criteria.why: One stormFront world with one caprock and one straw ground, and one hero station recurring on 1, 3, 6 (distant), 7 and 9. Camera moves around it, and the heads' pan evolves until they face the lens on 9. The interiors on 4, 5 and 8 are the declared cut, and 4 to 5 is a held camera with the page swapped, which works. Frame 8 sits outside the deck: no station, no plain, a different room from 4 and 5. The edge tease (road leaves 1, arrives at the gate on 9) is barely legible, because frame 1 shows a pad and hardly any road.

criteria.name: claim_integrity
criteria.why:
Traceable throughout, and the core spine (c8, c33, c34) is primary and verified against the snapshots. Four looser spots:
(1) Frame 8's headline 'Eight of 160 utilities had complied.' uses the Tribune's framing (c43) as the deck's own fact. c44 ('January is coming') and c45 (4 dated, 135 preparing, 13 silent) are in the claims file, show the filing window has not closed, and are on no surface, so a reader takes away 152 utilities out of compliance. It is also journalism where the hearing record exists.
(2) Frame 2 sources the fire's cause to the Tribune (c53) where an official investigation exists. It is attributed, so not a stretch.
(3) Frame 7's 'The cost was counted to the dollar.' sits over an ANTICIPATED $10,537,400, a figure rounded to hundreds, and the same report gives the ACTUAL 2025 camera capital spend only as 'approximately $2M'. So the precision the headline credits belongs to a projection.
(4) Frame 1's dek says 'Its approved plan lists' the metric, but the list is the order's Finding of Fact 49 (c33). The caption gets this right with 'Its order lists'.
The first comment cites the 57941 report with c8 c9 c10 c15 c21 c57 c58 but not c18 and c20, which carry the caption's 24 and 26. The source URL is present, so this is not a hard fail. The Tribune claims have no local snapshot, so frame 8's 'a hearing on wildfire mitigation plans' could not be checked beyond c43's quote.

criteria.name: story_and_stakes
criteria.why: A Texan learns what happened (the report answered the detections line with cameras), who (SPS as Xcel, the PUCT), where (most of the Panhandle), and when (May 1st, and the July 10th, 2025 order). Frame 9 gives Docket 57463 and Project 57941. The next step is weak. There is no comment route or deadline, and the 2027 report is named without its May 1st due date, which c58 supports. The fire stake on frame 2 is concrete. The cameras' own performance stays abstract by necessity.

criteria.name: sequence_and_momentum
criteria.why: The cover hook 'Agreed to count fire detections. Counted cameras.' earns the swipe. Frame 2 pays with Smokehouse Creek. The turn runs 4 to 5 to 6 (question, answer, filled and bare rails) and lands. Frame 7's money contrast is a real second beat. Frame 8 is the detour: a statewide count under a different rule that the dek has to explain away, and it could be cut with little loss. The close is a question, which lands.

criteria.name: voice
criteria.why: Clean, attributed and fair. It carries SPS's own partial-year caveat on 5 and says 'A missing count isn't a count of none' on 6. House rules hold: no colons outside verbatim quotes, 'can't', no year on May 1st, ordinals. Some lines read as filing prose rather than a Texan speaking, e.g. frame 9's 'The order sits in Docket 57463 and the report SPS filed on May 1st in Project 57941, both on the PUCT Interchange.' and frame 8's rule-distinction clause.

criteria.name: variety
criteria.why: stormFront light and a Panhandle caprock world are new against nos. 32 to 35, and the utility-filing instrument is not an ERCOT request or a governor's directive. The moves are familiar, though: the same rendered-kit look as the last four decks, a document-on-desk pair (frames 4 and 5), a figure at the close, and a spine built on a document's absence, which the topics ledger has asked runs to stop leaning on since no. 11.

one_sentence_fix: Rebuild frame 8 around 'had filed' rather than 'had complied', with c44's January deadline and c45's breakdown in the dek, so the one statewide number in the deck no longer tells a reader 152 utilities are breaking a law whose filing window the hearing itself said is still open. Then spend the next art round on frame 3's box heads and flat ground and on frame 6's heads, which don't render as the white housings they are meant to be.
